mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions for corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the month prior to the decision
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 24-month walk-forward, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.0% in any of the preceding 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE by at least 0.2 percentage points over the prior month is a leading indicator of labor market cooling, which precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month increase ≥ 0.2pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE rises by ≥0.2pp for ≥2 months, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% of instances (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) show a double-digit month-over-month increase, it signals a strengthening demand cycle that is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +10% and HOUST > +10% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where both proxies meet the trigger, the forward return is not positive in more than 40% of cases (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) by at least 5 points in the month prior to the decision, accompanied by a decline in RSAFS (retail sales), predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it reflects weak manufacturing and consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by ≥5 points AND RSAFS < previous month
regime_hint: early warning of soft landing failure
failure_condition: Over 30 consecutive 5-day windows with the trigger, the 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 70% of windows (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) for three consecutive months below 3% suggests deflationary pressure, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as investors anticipate lower inflation and rate cuts.
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL < 3.0 for ≥3 months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 10,000 in a month indicates labor market expansion that precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: In 12 consecutive 60-day windows where PAYEMS meets the trigger, the forward return is not positive in more than 50% (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent double-digit increases in HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) in the same month, but only during a period of falling UNRATE, signal a demand-led upturn that is associated with a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +10% AND HOUST > +10% AND UNRATE < previous month
regime_hint: demand expansion in labor slack period
failure_condition: During regimes matching the trigger condition, the 20-day forward return is not positive in more than 40% of windows (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in both INDPRO and GDPC1 by at least 8 points over two consecutive months indicates a supply-side shock that is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by ≥8 AND GDPC1 < previous month by ≥8 over two consecutive months
regime_hint: supply disruption or soft landing risk
failure_condition: In 50 such two-month windows, the 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% (binomial test).
